base_glossary: Total Cost of Ownership — full lifecycle cost: acquisition, possession, transformation, disposal.
Customer Order Decoupling Point — where you commit to specific demand (MTS / MTO / ATO / ETO).
Pareto-based SKU classification: A items (~80% value), B (~15%), C (~5%).
Forecast error metrics: Mean Absolute Deviation, Root Mean Squared Error, Mean Absolute Percent Error.
Demand variance amplification upstream. 4 causes: signal processing, rationing, batching, price fluctuation.
Sales & Operations Planning — monthly executive cadence aligning demand, supply, and finance.
Forecast method for intermittent demand; decouples size and inter-arrival time.
New-product diffusion with innovation (p) and imitation (q) coefficients.
Economic Order Quantity. Q* = √(2DS/H). Robust because cost curve is flat near optimum.
Single-period stocking under uncertain demand. Optimal quantile = Cu / (Cu + Co).
Inventory beyond cycle stock to absorb variance. SS = z · σ.
Multi-Echelon Technique for Recoverable Item Control. Pools risk across nodes.
Cycle Service Level (P[no stockout]) vs Fill Rate (E[fraction filled]).
2×2 spend segmentation by supply risk × profit impact: Routine, Leverage, Bottleneck, Strategic.
Transaction Cost Economics — Williamson's framework for make-vs-buy via asset specificity.
Strategic vs transactional segmentation. Different tiers warrant different relationship investment.
Splitting volume across two suppliers. Trades unit price for disruption-cost insurance.
Buyer-side competitive bidding. Works only for commoditized, multi-bidder, low-switch categories.
Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement. Your walk-away. Never reveal it.
Zone Of Possible Agreement. Overlap between buyer and seller reservation prices.
Contract aligning supplier compensation to buyer realization (Cachon-Lariviere).
Quantity Flexibility — pre-commit baseline + paid options for variation (Tsay).
Supplier repurchase of unsold inventory at fraction of cost (Pasternack).
Cost transparency between buyer and supplier. Margin becomes negotiated, not guessed.
Procurement & Operations Excellence Model — A.T. Kearney supplier maturity curve.
Failure Mode & Effects Analysis. RPN = Severity × Occurrence × Detection.
Facility location formulation: minimize weighted distance from demand to facilities.
Distribution facility with no inventory holding; flow-through only.
Vehicle Routing Problem. NP-hard combinatorial optimization for multi-stop routes.
Contract pricing tied to a published commodity index. Self-adjusting as market moves.
Mismatch between hedge instrument and physical exposure. Residual risk after hedging.
Volume discount applied retroactively to all units when threshold is crossed.
Single Point of Failure. A node whose disruption cascades to system collapse.
Recovery Time / Recovery Point Objectives. The two BCP numbers.
Software Bill of Materials. Cyber supply chain transparency.
Expected Value of Perfect Information. Maximum justifiable spend on info improvement.
Expected Value of Imperfect Information. EVPI scaled by quality.
Sensitivity diagram showing variables ranked by impact on outcome.
Simulation method using repeated random sampling to estimate distributions.
Volume, Variety, Variation, Visibility. Slack et al. operations strategy.
Theory of Constraints (Goldratt). Five focusing steps: identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate, repeat.
Toyota Production System. Pull, jidoka, heijunka, kanban. The basis for Lean.
Indirect emissions across the value chain. Categories 1 and 4 dominate.
Supply chain that designs out waste — reduce, reuse, refurbish, remanufacture, recycle.
Cost of Goods Sold. Aggregate TCO at the product level. Drives gross margin.
On-Time Delivery. Standard supplier scorecard metric.
Overall Equipment Effectiveness = Availability × Performance × Quality.
Minimum Order Quantity. Supplier-imposed lower bound; binding on EOQ.
Net Present Value. Time-discounted cash flows; canonical investment criterion.
Coefficient of Variation = σ / µ. Demand variability normalized.
new_glossary: TRIPLE-A
Hau Lee's framework: Agility, Adaptability, Alignment. Best supply chains have all three; alignment gates the others.
VALUE CAPTURE
Brandenburger-Stuart: the share of created value a firm appropriates. Distinct from value creation.
CAPABILITY
Pisano: a firm-specific bundle of routines and assets that competitors cannot easily replicate.
p-MEDIAN
MILP formulation: choose p facilities from candidates to minimize weighted distance to demand.
p-CENTER
MILP variant: minimize the maximum distance any customer travels (vs p-median which minimizes weighted average).
SET COVERING
Minimum number of facilities such that every demand point is within a radius (alternative to p-median).
MILP
Mixed-Integer Linear Programming. Workhorse of network design — combinatorial choices + linear constraints.
DUAL VARIABLE
In LP, the shadow price of a constraint. Reveals which constraints are binding and what they cost.
NP-HARD
Computational class. VRP, p-median, scheduling — all NP-hard. Practitioners use heuristics, not exact solvers.
SAVINGS ALGO
Clarke-Wright heuristic for VRP. Combines routes by selecting pairs that maximize distance saved.
LITTLE'S LAW
L = λ × W. Average inventory = throughput × time-in-system. Holds for any stable queueing system.
M/M/1
Single-server queue with Poisson arrivals and exponential service. Foundational queueing model.
ERLANG C
Multi-server queueing formula for call center / dock staffing. Predicts wait time given arrivals and service rate.
SCOPE 1/2/3
GHG emissions accounting: 1=direct (boilers), 2=purchased energy, 3=value chain (the 70–95% upstream).
CBAM
EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (2023). Prices imported carbon. Real cost on EU-bound supply chains.
EU ETS
EU Emissions Trading System. ~€80–100/tonne CO as of 2026. Foundational carbon market.
SBTi
Science Based Targets initiative. Validates corporate emissions targets against 1.5°C/2°C pathways.
CIRCULARITY
Designing supply chains for reuse, repair, remanufacturing. Ellen MacArthur Foundation taxonomy.
FRIEND-SHORING
Yellen 2022. Relocating production to politically aligned countries. Trades cost for geopolitical stability.
DECOUPLING
Reducing supply chain interdependence with geopolitical rival. US-China decoupling is the salient case.
CHIPS ACT
$200B+ US semiconductor industrial policy (2022). Largest peacetime industrial subsidy in US history.
IRA
Inflation Reduction Act (2022). $370B for clean energy + EV batteries with domestic content requirements.
SECTION 301
US trade law authorizing tariffs on China. ~25% on most categories since 2018; politically irreversible.
DSCSA
Drug Supply Chain Security Act. Mandates unit-level serialization + electronic chain-of-custody for US pharma.
EPCIS
Electronic Product Code Information Services. The data exchange standard underlying DSCSA.
COLD CHAIN
Temperature-controlled supply chain (typically 2–8°C for vaccines, ≤−15°C for some biologics).
FDA 483
FDA notice of objectionable conditions during inspection. Operations-stopping event for regulated facilities.
EUV
Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography. ASML monopoly. Gates ≤7nm semiconductor production.
FOUNDRY
Pure-play semiconductor manufacturer (TSMC, Samsung Foundry). Distinct from IDMs (Intel) and fabless (Nvidia).
ALLOCATION
When fab capacity is constrained, the share each customer receives. A queueing problem with priority rules.
BEER GAME
Sterman 1989 simulation showing bullwhip emerges even with rational players due to feedback misperception.
ANCHORING
Tversky-Kahneman 1974. First number framing dominates subsequent estimates. First-offer effect in negotiation.
